_ceiling_note: ceiling_usd caps the ADJUDICATOR (gemini) spend only. Executor spend is capped per cycle by cycle_budget_usd on the sdk channel.
_channel_note: MUST be sdk for P5. The ahk channel is a machine-wide singleton keyed on claude_window_title, so a concurrent run on that channel would prove nothing about the thing P5 exists to test.
_lanes_note: Machine-wide cap on concurrent executor calls across ALL callers (RC + Sibling-A), enforced via C:/ProgramData/lw-loop/slots. Both repos MUST agree on this number.
_ignore_no_progress_note: true on purpose: the P5 scope is one appended line per cycle, and the same-sha guard is not what is under test here.
cycle_command: P5 CONCURRENT-RUN SMOKE, Tier-0 docs only, RC repo. Read ops/loop/control/cycle.txt for cycle number N. Append EXACTLY ONE line to docs/_archive/2026-07-26-p5-concurrent-smoke.md (create with a one-line heading if absent), of the form: "- RC cycle N: <one sentence on what you observed> (head <8-char sha before your commit>)". STRICT SCOPE: touch NO other file, and NEVER any path under C:/Sibling-A. No code changes. 7-bit ASCII only, no em-dashes or smart quotes. Then git add that one file, commit with a conventional-commit subject, push to origin main.
_cycle_command_note: cycle_command, NOT fixed_directive. fixed_directive skips BOTH the director and the auditor, so no gemini call ever happens and P5 condition 4 (gemini windows never overlap) would pass VACUOUSLY by doing nothing. cycle_command skips only the director and KEEPS the auditor, so every cycle makes a real gemini call through GEMINI_MUTEX - which is the thing condition 4 measures.
